claims.text: Failure modes and idempotency: loading the table is a pure read of packaged bytes (lru_cache), and categorising writes nothing, so a re-run gives the same result. There are no external calls, so the timeout and retry lines do not apply. On partial failure, a damaged, missing or changed table, or a missing rules package, is refused before anything is recorded. A legacy resume with a damaged table leaves the review pending, and the same review resumes once the table is repaired.

Data, migration and rollback: the change is additive. The evidence gains a ruleset key, the graph state gains an optional ruleset, and CHECKPOINT_TYPES is unchanged. It is reversible in both directions against real SQLite checkpoints. A review left pending by fd7b64c resumes here, and a review left pending here resumes under fd7b64c, which is the rollback by reinstalling the previous wheel. There is no backfill. No PII is added: evidence gets an id and a hash only.
Packaging: the built wheel carries v1.yaml byte for byte. Loaded from outside the checkout, it gives the source file's hash.

Dependencies and secrets: the change adds no dependency, because pyyaml>=6 was already a runtime dependency. The only pyproject change is the pytest markers. No secrets appear in the changed code, the table or the test tools.

notes: No code change was needed in this pass, because c16ddb7 already addresses all three verify-12 findings and the escalation guidance. Gaps for the owner: (1) The repo has no CHANGELOG, so there is no release-note line. Adding a changelog is a project decision, not part of T01. (2) There is no remote alert, by design (local-first, design.md Observability). The refusal with exit 2 is the alert, and no runbook file exists to add an entry to. (3) The P7 history and wheel tests need git with fd7b64c reachable (CI uses fetch-depth 0) and pip able to build a wheel. In a shallow clone, test_p7_history skips instead of failing. (4) FROZEN_SHA256 makes any edit to v1.yaml, including comment-only and CRLF edits, a refusal. This is intended, but it means a fix to v1 must ship as a new table id.
